about.title: About Loan Calculator
about.description: The Loan Calculator helps you estimate monthly payments, total interest costs, and amortization schedules for many fixed-rate loans. Whether it's a mortgage, auto loan, personal loan, or business loan, this tool supports side-by-side review of loan terms and repayment scenarios. Use it to compare borrowing costs and budget impact before choosing a loan offer.

faq.q: What's included in the monthly loan payment calculation?
faq.a: The basic loan calculator includes principal and interest (P&I) payments. For mortgages, you may need to add property taxes, homeowners insurance, and PMI separately for the total monthly housing payment. Our calculator focuses on the core loan payment components.

faq.q: How does the loan term affect my monthly payments?
faq.a: Longer loan terms result in lower monthly payments but higher total interest costs over the loan lifetime. Shorter terms mean higher monthly payments but significant interest savings. Our loan calculator helps you compare different term options to find the right balance.

faq.q: Can I calculate the impact of making extra loan payments?
faq.a: Yes, the calculator shows how additional principal payments may change the loan term and total interest. The effect depends on the balance, interest rate, term, and payment amount you enter.

faq.q: What's the difference between interest rate and APR?
faq.a: Interest rate is the basic cost of borrowing the principal amount. APR (Annual Percentage Rate) includes the interest rate plus additional fees and costs like origination fees, giving you a more complete annual borrowing-cost reference. Use APR when comparing loan offers.

faq.q: What types of loans can I calculate with this tool?
faq.a: Our loan calculator works for many fixed-rate loans including auto loans, personal loans, student loans, business loans, and mortgages. Enter the loan amount, interest rate, and term to review estimated payment calculations.

faq.q: How should I interpret the loan payment calculations?
faq.a: The calculator uses standard amortization formulas to provide payment estimates. Actual loan costs can vary due to rounding, fees, escrow items, insurance, taxes, or lender-specific calculation methods.
